To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of DSP techniques in the analysis of power traces is an efficient and effective way of improving the effectiveness of differential-power attacks, and that it is possible to extract a leakage model of the software implementation of AES from a single power trace.

the leakage model for software AES can be described as a linear combination of two functions, and the pre-processing technique can be applied to the leakage model to improve the effectiveness and the efficiency of the attacks.

(1) the leakage model for software implementations is the sum of the leakage model of each instruction, weighted by the probability of occurrence of that instruction; (2) a DSP pre-processing technique, based on the use of a Kalman filter, is able to reduce the amount of data needed to perform an efficient attack by one order of magnitude; (3) the proposed technique is applicable to any software implementation, and can be applied in a completely automated fashion.
